# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial – Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)**
**Member:** Reese Iverson
**Member ID:** W233165693
**Reference Number:** POC-757C3B7E16-21498
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-06
**Payer:** Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana (Commercial/ACA)

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), which was denied on 2026-08-06 for the stated reason that the clinical records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary, and I believe the record shows that I have already completed extensive conservative treatment.

## The Governing Policy

I understand this request was reviewed under **Carelon Joint Surgery 2025-11-15 (HTML)** (https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/), effective 2025-11-15, which is the guideline your plan uses through Carelon for musculoskeletal surgery review.

## Mapping My Records to the Plan's Own Language

The guideline excerpts provided to me state, as one element of the conservative-care standard for shoulder procedures:

> "Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks' duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes)"

I want to be transparent that this specific sentence appears in the portion of the guideline addressing hemiarthroplasty, not in a section specifically labeled for rotator cuff repair. I have not been given the exact rotator cuff repair section of the guideline, so I am not able to quote plan language that applies word-for-word to CPT 29827. I am asking the plan to identify and provide that specific section (see request below). That said, if a 6-week conservative-care threshold is any guide to what the plan considers adequate, my records show far more than that:

- I have had progressive shoulder pain for **18 months**, unrelieved by rest.
- I completed **16 weeks of supervised physical therapy** (2026-02-24 to 2026-06-16, 16 visits), focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took **NSAIDs for 8 months** with inadequate relief.
- I received a **corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-30**, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- An **MRI on 2026-07-07** confirmed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- I currently cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side, and my exam shows positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion.

This is a documented, multi-modality course of conservative treatment lasting well over a year, not a matter of weeks. I do not have an active infection, untreated substance use, or any of the contraindications the guideline lists elsewhere. I ask the plan to explain, specifically, what additional conservative treatment it believes was required and to identify where in its own published criteria for rotator cuff repair (as distinct from arthroplasty) that requirement appears.

## Request for the Criteria Applied

Because Carelon publishes its Joint Surgery, Spine Surgery, and Small Joint Surgery guidelines publicly with no login required, I am asking the plan to provide, in writing, the specific criteria section it applied to CPT 29827 in my case — including the conservative-care standard specific to rotator cuff repair, if one differs from what has been shared with me — so that I can respond to the actual basis for the denial.

## Deadline and Submission

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-02-02** (180 days from the date of this notice). I am submitting this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, or, if that is unclear, to the appeals address confirmed by calling the number on the back of my insurance card.

## What I Am Asking

I am asking the plan to reverse this denial and approve the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) recommended by my surgeon, based on the conservative treatment I have already completed and documented. If the plan is not able to approve the request on the record as submitted, I ask that it identify precisely what is missing under its own published criteria.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

________________________________
Reese Iverson
Member ID: W233165693

[Contact address]
